title: Compute-Matched Evaluation of Transform-Augmented GRPO for Mathematical Reasoning

contributions.purpose: Determine whether TA-GRPO's reported gains over standard GRPO come from its semantic transformation mechanism or merely from 4x more rollouts.
contributions.mechanism: A compute-matched evaluation where standard GRPO (708 steps, 8 rollouts/prompt) and TA-GRPO (177 steps, 32 rollouts/prompt group) consume identical total rollouts (~725K).
contributions.evaluation: Under identical rollout budgets TA-GRPO achieves +2.02pp higher Pass@32 than GRPO-Long (49.47% vs 47.45%), confirming genuine benefits beyond additional compute.
contributions.source_quote: We present the first compute-matched evaluation of TA-GRPO, demonstrating that it achieves +2.02pp higher Pass@32 than GRPO-Long under identical rollout budgets, confirming that semantic transformations provide genuine benefits beyond additional compute.

contributions.purpose: Decompose TA-GRPO's improvement into its two constituent mechanisms.
contributions.mechanism: An ablation condition that uses transformations but computes advantages per-variant rather than pooled, isolating data augmentation from pooled advantage normalization.
contributions.evaluation: 87% of TA-GRPO's improvement comes from semantic data augmentation, while only 13% comes from pooled advantage normalization.
contributions.source_quote: Through ablation analysis, we show that 87% of TA-GRPO's improvement comes from semantic data augmentation, while only 13% comes from pooled advantage normalization.

contributions.purpose: Characterize how TA-GRPO's advantage scales with inference-time compute.
contributions.mechanism: Pass@k scaling and variance-rescue analysis across k = 1 to 32.
contributions.evaluation: TA-GRPO's advantage grows with inference-time compute, from +1.07pp at k = 1 to +2.02pp at k = 32, consistent with improved solution diversity.
contributions.source_quote: We analyze Pass@k scaling and variance rescue, finding that TA-GRPO's advantage grows with inference-time compute (from +1.07pp at k = 1 to +2.02pp at k = 32), consistent with improved solution diversity.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Recently, Transform-Augmented GRPO (TA-GRPO) (Le et al., 2026) extended this approach by generating semantically equivalent variants of each training prompt through paraphrasing, variable renaming, and format changes, then pooling advantages across the entire group.
In this paper, we design a compute-matched evaluation to isolate the true contribution of semantic transformations.

notes: Pure re-evaluation/analysis paper of an existing method (TA-GRPO); all three contributions are findings, no new method proposed. Related Work section not on pages 1-2 (Section 2 is Method).
